searchText: What's the reason for not running a full client on a mobile device after The Merge? Wym by full client? I mean like a full node Running a full execution + consensus client would require the similar amount of storage and network bandwidth similar to that of current full node. This is not possible to run on a mobile devide because of battery life and computation? mainnet execution clients require hundreds of GBs of storage. The RAM might be there, though they typically want 16GB of RAM and mobile platforms such as Android and iOS are loathe to allow individual processes to use that. etc I assumed that after the merge, and after shards will be introduced, a full node will require less computation power Whatever the future situation, the immediate post-merge situation won't have sharding (there are other EIPs addressing what sharding is/was supposed to) Have anyone from the FE ever addressed the potential of having full nodes executed on mobile phones? assuming the technical limitations you mentioned would be resolved? yes I know. I don't know, it's a good question to ask them What channel to use then? probably this one There are very smart people working on trying to make it so one can run a light client on a mobile device, namely the Portal Network. Are these the guys you were mentioning? 🙂 Just kidding of course, ok thanks. I'll dig deeper to the Portal Network tech. BBS thanks 🙂 With the most compact current methods, it is now feasible store the Mainnet execution state database, pruned (recent 90k blocks worth), in a modern mobile phone's storage, even without sharding or the Portal Network DHT. Storing block bodies in Portal reduces the space needed, and that's the simplest part of Portal I think (the block bodies are effectively just simple files without complicated latency requirements or structure). But the battery will be drained if it's trying to keep up with the network. The computations are too intensive to run all day, and the constant radio communications will also drain the battery. Above was a reply to your question, forgot to link it as a reply 🙂 I understand, although it is possible, IMHO, that future layers will be able to execute on mobile devices and support the “Decentralized Internet”. Something like what Handshake is doing
